messages:
incidentbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service=redwood-gpu-hosts-prod, severity=critical. Trigger: kubelet NotReady on host gpu-node-12-az3. Auto-page to eng-oncall rotation.

alexa: acked. seeing node disappear from kube-api. trying `kubectl get nodes | grep gpu-node-12`

sam: seeing CPU/IO spike in metrics, kubelet heartbeat stopped ~12:03 UTC. mmm nvme io errors in host logs?

alexa: pulling host serial logs, connecting via BMC console now. attaching snippet: ```kernel: nvme0: I/O 0 QID 0 timeout, aborting````

opsbot: automated action: created incident ticket INC-20240315-482. linked to pagerduty. snapshotting metrics and recent pod schedules.

maria: quick customer impact check — are any production jobs pinned to that node? I see some long-running inference pods were on that rack.

sam: loadbalancer health shows a handful of 504s hitting inference-route A over last 4m. likely those pods were on gpu-node-12. routing should failover but burst caused queueing.

alexa: can confirm two replicas were on that node: `redwood-infer-prod-8` and `batch-encoder-3`. I started a quick reschedule: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-12 && kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`

jin: if drain hangs, we should force delete stuck pods and let HPA recreate. Also check dedicated device-plugin state, NVidia plugin tends to hang when node kernel hits NVMe errors.

kevin: echoing jin. here's command I use if drain blocks on device-plugin: ```kubectl get pod -n kube-system -o wide | grep device-plugin && kubectl delete pod <stuck-pod> -n kube-system```

alexa: cordon succeeded, drain stuck on `redwood-infer-prod-8` with `Terminating` for >2m. trying force delete now.

incidentbot: pagerduty: alert escalated to level-2 oncall (sam) after 5 minutes with no mitigation complete.

sam: I'm on it. removing finalizer from adapter and `kubectl delete pod redwood-infer-prod-8 --grace-period=0 --force`. pods recreating on healthy nodes.

maria: customer-impact update: we saw a ~0.8% error spike in prod traffic window, mostly retries handled by clients. notified Product to watch SLAs, but no customer-facing outage page needed at this time.

jin: ops note — devices on that host show `NVMe SMART` errors, possibly failing SSD. suggest RMA. tagging infra team.

alexa: host serial shows kernel oops before kubelet stopped: `kernel: BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference` then hang. collecting `dmesg` and `journalctl -u kubelet` logs, uploading to incident ticket.

opsbot: added runbook checklist to ticket: "cordon -> drain -> force-delete -> verify pods -> check LB -> open infra RMA".

kevin: checking RBAC/eviction limits: if many pods land on same node we might hit node allocatable issues. looks ok for this incident.

sam: lowering noise: silencing repeated nvme alerts for node gpu-node-12 in cloudwatch for 30m to avoid alert fatigue while infra investigates.

maria: tagging support: any customer escalations? support: none open yet, monitoring.

alexa: status summary for handoff: node gpu-node-12 had kernel oops + NVMe errors -> kubelet NotReady -> drained/cordoned -> critical pods force-deleted and rescheduled -> minor customer error spike (~0.8%) -> infra RMA opened. logs + ticket INC-20240315-482 attached.

jin: I'm taking over on-call for the next 30m to watch for regressions and confirm RMA progress. leave any follow-ups here. :eyes:

incidentbot: note: oncall handoff recorded: alexa -> jin at 12:14 UTC. pagerduty incident remains open pending infra RMA and postmortem.

kevin: created quick dashboard panel showing node-level NVMe errors + pod reschedule rate. good for postmortem graphs.

maria: thanks team. I'll draft a brief customer-impact blurb if infra confirms RMA. otherwise minimal follow-up.

jin: will keep thread updated, closing active mitigation. next steps in ticket.

alexa: thanks all. :thumbsup:
